timingStatus: Normal active intervals and total durations compared with UFD and current definitions. This is planning data, not runtime-loaded configuration.
poseStatus: Authored 2D pose proposals. Source GIF URLs are recorded, but full motion/handedness review is required per batch before generation; no native skeletal reconstruction is claimed.
frameConvention: One-based inclusive from/to; charge holds, hitlag, landing and conditional branches are outside the uninterrupted base timeline.

delivery.facing: fighter faces right; rear attacks extend left
delivery.registration: Fixed simulation origin; pelvis and feet may move intentionally with the pose. Do not auto-center alpha bounds or rescale individual poses.

globals.poseReferences: Use each clip's sourceAnimationUrl for motion, not costume/style.
invariants: Match current green tunic, dark green cape, blond hair, pointed ears, boots, silver sword with blue/gold hilt, and blue shield identity.
Preserve body proportions and equipment length across poses.
No baked collision overlays, projectiles, text, labels, scenery, floor shadows or checkerboard transparency.
Do not change damage, active windows, charge timing or collision to accommodate drawings.

poses.instruction: Right-facing guard; load the first short forward sword strike with a small shoulder turn.
Draw the sword hand back into the first strike's anticipation; keep the planted stance readable.
First forward sword contact; extend the weapon clearly beyond the body without changing its length.
Release the first strike and begin retracting the arm; no contact remains.
Reach a distinct chain-ready guard that can connect to jab 2, with or without a new input.
Settle toward idle if no follow-up starts; do not draw an automatic second strike.

conditionalEvents.event: Earliest jab-2 transition if input accepted; interrupt recovery.

poses.instruction: Begin from the first jab's handoff pose; prepare a visibly different second sword motion.
Compact second-strike anticipation with consistent weapon grip and body scale.
Second forward sword contact, distinct in shoulder and blade silhouette from jab 1.
Release the second strike; no hitbox is active.
Chain-ready pose for jab 3; keep the sword available for the finishing motion.
Recover to guard if the chain ends.

conditionalEvents.event: Earliest jab-3 transition if input accepted; interrupt recovery.

poses.instruction: Continue from jab 2 with a stronger finisher preparation.
Load the finishing sword strike with an identifiable silhouette; preserve stance/root registration.
Finishing sword contact with full readable extension; confirm the exact blade path from the linked motion before generation.
Follow through after contact; do not repeat the impact pose as another strike.
Retract the sword and unwind the torso.
Return to a stable guard and match the idle proportions.
Begin a deliberate sword raise from grounded guard.
Prepare an overhead-to-forward sword sweep; shoulders and blade clearly above the initial guard.
Overhead contact pose: the blade must visibly threaten above the body.
Move the blade through the forward portion of the same sweep.
Finish the forward contact arc without creating a second strike.
Follow through and retract, with no contact.
Settle back into guard.

clips.label: Up tilt

poses.instruction: Grounded right-facing guard; soften the knees and prepare an upward sword sweep. Shield remains on the off arm.
Raise the sword into anticipation beside the shoulder; feet remain planted and the weapon arc has clear overhead space.
First active key of the overhead sweep. Match the blade direction at source frame 8; do not substitute a horizontal forward jab.
Next distinct active key, advancing the blade smoothly along the reference arc with unchanged sword length.
Middle active key: strong readable overhead silhouette; keep the face, shoulder and hilt identifiable.
Next active key beyond the middle of the arc, with continuous shoulder and wrist motion.
Last active key at the sweep exit; preserve the reference's front/rear ordering rather than guessing it.
Recover from the overhead sweep and bring the sword toward guard; no attack region remains.
Settle into the same body proportions and grounded anchor as idle.

clips.posePathStatus: Timing checked; source GIF motion direction must be visually checked before submitting the pilot.

poses.instruction: Lower into a grounded stance while retaining the same registered root and body scale.
Prepare a low sword sweep; keep the blade and hands clear of the shins.
Sweep low and forward near ground level; use the reference for the diagonal blade path.
Retract from the low strike without drawing an aerial plunge.
Rise toward the normal grounded guard.
Running approach pose transitioning into a committed sword attack; translation belongs to the simulation.
Load the running/lunging strike with a different silhouette from stationary forward tilt.
First part of running sword contact; readable forward reach and stable weapon proportions.
Finish the same contact arc; preserve one strike identity.
Forward momentum in the body pose, with the root still registered to its fixed canvas origin.
Recover balance and retract the sword.
Return to guard; do not slide the artwork across its canvas to mimic travel.
Load a strong grounded forward sword swing.
Reusable charge-hold pose: visibly loaded and stable for a variable duration.
Release from the hold into the strike anticipation.
Strong forward sword contact with a readable blade tip; do not bake a sword beam into the body image.
Follow through and begin preparing the optional second swing.
Recovery/handoff posture that can transition to the separately generated smash2 sequence.
Finish recovery to idle when no second swing occurs.

conditionalEvents.event: Earliest optional smash2 transition. Current closing frame 36 is project calibration.
Sword beam is a separate conditional entity at 0% damage; keep it out of body art.

clips.label: Forward smash 2

poses.instruction: Begin from the first swing's handoff, never from an unrelated idle pose.
Prepare the distinct follow-up sword swing.
Second swing contact, clearly different from forward smash 1.
Large finishing follow-through with no additional contact.
Retract and regain balance.
Long final recovery toward guard.

clips.entryCondition: Only after an accepted follow-up input during smash1; never append automatically.

poses.instruction: Prepare a grounded upward multi-sweep attack.
Stable charge-hold pose for the overhead attack.
Release into the first overhead sweep.
First overhead contact arc, with a distinctive blade angle.
Exit the first contact arc; retain the same strike identity.
Harmless transition into the second sweep; no active hitbox.
Second overhead contact arc, visibly distinct from the first.
Exit the second contact arc.
Harmless transition and preparation for the finishing sweep.
Third, finishing overhead contact arc with a stronger extension.
Lower the sword and recover from the finisher.
Return to guard.

clips.label: Down smash

poses.instruction: Crouch and load a grounded low sweep.
Stable low charge-hold pose.
Prepare the front sweep, keeping the physical root registered.
Low front contact: sword extends toward screen-right for a right-facing fighter.
Release front contact and begin turning the torso.
Harmless transition toward the rear sweep; no hitbox.
Low rear contact: sword extends screen-left relative to the same right-facing fighter reference.
Recover from the rear sweep with continuous torso motion.
Return to grounded guard.

clips.facingNote: New sequence uses fighter-facing coordinates. Current rear-window sprite flip must be reconciled during integration to avoid mirroring twice.

poses.instruction: Airborne preparation for a kick; sword is carried safely and is not the striking limb.
Extend the kicking leg while bending the supporting leg for a readable airborne silhouette.
Clear initial extended-kick contact; foot/leg is the striking region.
Sustain the kick with consistent limb length and body orientation.
Continue the same late kick, allowing restrained cloth motion without a new impact.
Retract the leg into airborne recovery.
Airborne sword preparation with a stable registered root.
Load the first forward slash.
First forward sword contact.
Release the first slash with no contact.
Prepare the second slash during the harmless gap.
Distinct second forward sword contact.
Follow through after the second slash.
Retract into airborne guard; landing may interrupt this sequence.

clips.label: Back air

poses.instruction: Airborne preparation for a rear kick; fighter reference remains facing screen-right.
Load the first kick behind the body; do not turn it into a forward sword attack.
First rear kick extending toward screen-left.
Retract the first kick during the harmless gap.
Load the distinct second rear kick.
Second rear kick toward screen-left, with a distinct leg/hip silhouette.
Retract the leg and recover airborne balance.
Return to airborne guard.

clips.facingNote: Author in fighter-facing coordinates; current reversed aerial attack axis must not mirror the new rear-kick art twice.

poses.instruction: Prepare the sword above the airborne body.
Align the blade for an upward thrust, with hands and hilt below its point.
Initial upward thrust; blade points upward rather than lying horizontally across the head.
Sustain the overhead thrust as the body moves with the simulation.
Continue the same late thrust with restrained cloth/limb adjustment and no extra attack.
Retract the sword from overhead.
Recover into airborne guard.
Prepare the sword underneath the airborne body.
Aim the blade downward, bringing limbs clear of the plunge.
Initial downward sword plunge; blade is visibly beneath the body.
Sustain the downward thrust; simulation supplies movement, not canvas translation.
Continue the late downward thrust as one strike identity.
Retract the blade when ordinary recovery begins.
Recover to airborne guard; landing or rebound can branch earlier.

conditionalEvents.event: Successful rebound uses a separate branch/return pose; do not play it unconditionally or infer it from elapsed time.

contactGroupConvention: Explicit hitWindows group names match Link.ts. For moves without explicit windows, strike labels the single ordinary hit for planning only.
